run.question:
In the cluster's elasticsearch I have three log indices for app-280
that I need to query. Please answer all three of the following:

1. In index 'app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3', run a `term: { level: "ERROR" }`
   query and report the count. If that returns zero, find the right
   field and re-run.

2. In index 'app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3', run a `terms: { level: ["ERROR",
   "FATAL"] }` query and report the count. If that returns zero, find
   the right field for severity and re-run.

3. In index 'app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3', run a range query on
   `@timestamp` for today's date and filter to ERROR-level entries,
   and report the count. If the @timestamp filter returns zero or
   errors, find the right timestamp field and re-run.

report.summary: All three named indices exist (16, 13 and 16 docs respectively) but each uses a different schema, so the field names in the question only work in index c. (1) app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 has no `level` field; `term: {level: "ERROR"}` returned 0, and on the severity-equivalent field `severity`, `term: {severity: "ERROR"}` also returned 0 with an empty severity bucket aggregation over the full authorized window; a match_all query on that index over the same window returned no documents, so the severity split of its 16 stored documents was not observed. (2) app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 has no `level` and no string severity field; `terms: {level: ["ERROR","FATAL"]}` returned 0, and the correct field is the integer `severity_num` (3=INFO, 5=ERROR, 6=FATAL), where `terms: {severity_num: [5,6]}` returned 8 over the authorized window (6 ERROR + 2 FATAL). (3) app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 has no `@timestamp` (its time field is the keyword `ingest_ts`); the @timestamp range query returned 0, and a corrected range on ingest_ts for 2026-11-21 combined with `level: ERROR` returned 7.

claims.text: Index app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 maps only @timestamp (date), message (text), service (keyword) and severity (keyword): it has no `level` field, so the severity-equivalent field is `severity`.
In app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3, `term: {level: "ERROR"}` returned total 0 (relation eq) for the window 2026-11-21T08:06:56Z–2026-11-21T09:06:56Z with 0 failed shards.

Re-running on the correctly named field, `term: {severity: "ERROR"}` in app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 also returned total 0 for the full authorized window 2026-11-20T09:06:56Z–2026-11-21T09:06:56Z, and the accompanying terms aggregation on `severity` returned an empty bucket list with sum_other_doc_count 0, i.e. the aggregation covered zero matched documents.
Index app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 maps @timestamp (date), msg (text), severity_num (integer) and svc (keyword); it has neither a `level` field nor a string `severity` field.
In app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3, `terms: {level: ["ERROR","FATAL"]}` returned total 0 for the window 2026-11-21T08:06:56Z–2026-11-21T09:06:56Z.

Over the full authorized window, app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 contains 13 documents whose severity_num values are 3 (5 docs), 5 (6 docs) and 6 (2 docs); the returned documents show msg '[INFO] healthcheck N' with severity_num 3, '[ERROR] DB timeout N' with 5 and '[FATAL] Disk full N' with 6, all svc=order-280.

The corrected query `terms: {severity_num: [5, 6]}` (ERROR + FATAL) in app-280-logs-b-p6t1z8k3 returned total 8 for the authorized window 2026-11-20T09:06:56Z–2026-11-21T09:06:56Z, consistent with the 6 ERROR plus 2 FATAL documents of that index.
Index app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 maps ingest_ts (keyword), level (keyword) and message (text); it has no `@timestamp` and no date-typed field, so the search tool applied no time filter for this index.

In app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3, the requested range on `@timestamp` (2026-11-21T00:00:00Z–2026-11-21T09:06:56Z) plus `term: {level: "ERROR"}` returned total 0, and the tool reported time_filter applied=false with field null because no matched index maps a date field.

The corrected query on the keyword time field, `range: {ingest_ts: {gte: "2026-11-21T00:00:00", lte: "2026-11-21T23:59:59"}}` AND `term: {level: "ERROR"}`, in app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 returned total 7.

app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 holds 16 documents with level buckets ERROR=12 and INFO=4; reading all 16 shows 7 ERROR on 2026-11-21 (ingest_ts 08:01–08:07, 'err today 1..7'), 5 ERROR on 2026-11-20 (08:01–08:05, 'err yest 1..5') and 4 INFO on 2026-11-21 (09:01–09:04, 'info today 1..4').

The zero result in app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 is most plausibly explained by its 16 documents falling outside the authorized window on @timestamp (or not carrying @timestamp at all) rather than by an absence of ERROR-severity documents; this is unverified because the match_all query over the full 24h window returned no documents.

If the severity split of app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 matters, query it without the tool's mandatory @timestamp window filter (for example the Elasticsearch API directly with a wide range, or after confirming which date field its documents actually populate) instead of re-running the same windowed query.

gaps: app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3: a match_all query over the full authorized window 2026-11-20T09:06:56Z–2026-11-21T09:06:56Z returned no documents (that view's status was no_data, so it cannot be cited as a fact), so it is unknown whether its 16 documents lie outside that window or lack @timestamp; their severity values were never observed and the reported 0 for severity=ERROR is limited to the queried window.
app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3: no severity distribution was ever listed, so non-standard values of its `severity` field (e.g. lowercase) remain unverified.

app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 has no date-typed field (ingest_ts is keyword), so the tool could not time-filter it: the 7-ERROR count was produced by a lexicographic range on ISO-like strings without timezone offset (e.g. '2026-11-21T08:01:00') and cannot be tied to the incident window by the tool; documents in another format would not be counted.

One delivered view of app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 was marked incomplete (34f438c6-7241-4fbb-a215-bbcf66e75064-t2:a01d2d06-86a5-4908-ad6f-7e1131bcb160: 16 matched, 5 shown); the full contents were later read in a separate view, so no gap remains for the level split.
Whether indices a, b and c belong to the same application or overlap in content beyond the naming pattern was not established.
next_steps: Inspect app-280-logs-a-p6t1z8k3 outside the tool's mandatory @timestamp window (direct API query or an unbounded date range) to confirm its @timestamp values and its `severity` value vocabulary before concluding it holds no ERROR entries.
Confirm with the index owner whether ingest_ts in app-280-logs-c-p6t1z8k3 is UTC and whether a date-typed field could be added so time filtering and Kibana range queries work.
